summary: After two iterations, the best Max-Cut score is 87.28 (out of 100), achieved by both the iter-1 SA-only (20 restarts) and iter-2 SA+ILS (12 restarts + perturbation) approaches. The TLE hypothesis that motivated iteration 2 was refuted — the iter-1 solution runs consistently with zero variance, and the original 84.62 score was a one-time anomaly. We are near the theoretical Goemans-Williamson bound of ~87.8%, so further gains require fundamentally different techniques.
key_points: Best score: 87.28/100, stable across repeated runs with both SA-only (20 restarts) and SA+ILS (12 restarts + perturbation). The two approaches are essentially tied.

Iteration 2's core hypothesis — that TLE caused iter-1's 84.62 score and ILS would fix it — was fully refuted. The iter-1 SA solution scores 87.28 consistently; the 84.62 was an anomaly (likely different test cases or judge-side issue).

Approaches tried and failed: Kernighan-Lin refinement (84.0, TLE from O(n²)), tabu search (44.4, too slow), SA with reheating (84.0, TLE), 40 short restarts (84.4), adaptive restarts (84.0). None beat the simple multi-restart SA baseline.

At 87.28% cut ratio vs the 87.8% GW theoretical bound, we're within 0.5% of the approximation ceiling. Next iteration should explore: (1) bucket-based O(1) tabu search for better move selection, (2) pair-swap moves to escape single-flip local optima, (3) SDP-inspired spectral initialization to start SA from better initial solutions.
Risk: diminishing returns are likely. Moving from 87.28 to 88+ may require SDP relaxation or highly optimized exact methods that are complex to implement within time limits.
